what: `PHI2 SELECT`: the CPU clock, 1 MHz (pins 1 and 2) or 2 MHz (pins 2 and 3).
do: Fit the shunt on pins 1 and 2, 1 MHz: at 2 MHz the sound chip, whose clock is always 1 MHz, answers only every other cycle. With no shunt the CPU has no clock.

what: `PHI2 SELECT`: the CPU clock, 1 MHz (pins 1 and 2) or 2 MHz (pins 2 and 3).
do: Fit the shunt on pins 1 and 2, 1 MHz, the speed every AC6502 is tested at. Pins 2 and 3 run the CPU, VIA, ACIA and sound chip at 2 MHz together, at the builder's risk: see *Clock*. With no shunt the CPU has no clock.

Fit the shunt on pins 1 and 2, ground, as the boards are built. On pins 2 and 3 it takes `CTS` from the cable, and a cable that doesn't assert it stops the transmitter. With no shunt the input floats, and serial may not work.

Fit the shunt on pins 1 and 2, ground, as the boards are built. On pins 2 and 3 it takes `DCD` from the cable, and a cable that doesn't assert it stops the receiver. With no shunt the input floats, and serial may not work.

what: Options for the ACIA's crystal: JP1 puts R38 (1M) across it, and JP2 adds C32 (22pF) to ground.
do: Leave them open for the R6551AP, the part the board is tested with. Close both for a Rockwell R65C51P1 or R65C51P2, whose oscillator won't start on the bare crystal (an R65C51P2 ran clean this way on a Serial Card on 2026-11-11), or for a WDC W65C51.
